summary.headline: J&K Bank posts FY26 net profit of INR2,363 crores, a fourth straight record, with Q4 profit near INR800 crores (up 36% QoQ); FY27 NIM guided at ~3.5%.
summary.overview: FY26 delivered a record annual net profit of INR2,363 crores and a record quarterly profit of nearly INR800 crores, up 36% QoQ. Business grew 13.6%, with advances up 16.8% and deposits up 11.3%, both above guidance. NIM for FY26 was 3.60%, a marginal miss against guidance, attributed to 125 bps of RBI rate cuts in 2025 and deposit competition. Operating expenses fell about 4%, and GNPA/NNPA stood at 2.50%/0.64%. FY27 guidance is conservative: credit growth 12%, deposits 10%, NIM about 3.5%, RoA maintained, RoE about 16%, GNPA below 2.25%.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR734 crores in Q4 FY25; includes INR153 crore one-off reversal

financial_highlights.value: INR180 crore impairment on EDB amalgamation into J&K Gramin Bank

segments.name: Jammu, Kashmir & Ladakh (J&K)
segments.commentary: Loan growth 9.5% in FY26 versus 28.8% in Rest of India; J&K & Ladakh share of loan book is 63% versus 37% for Rest of India as on 31 March 2026. Bank holds about 60% market share but only 37% branch share.

segments.name: Rest of India
segments.commentary: Loan growth 28.8% in FY26 under the recalibrated strategy; Personal loans grew above 13%, with housing and education loans growing double digits.

segments.name: Corporate and Agriculture
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 38.5% and Agriculture 27.6% in FY26. Financial market book (mainly AAA-rated NBFCs) rose sharply to about INR20,000 crores, with co-lending still immaterial.

segments.name: Retail, Agriculture & MSME (RAM)
segments.commentary: RAM remains more than two-thirds of the loan book. Car loans grew 17.5% and were the best-performing personal loan segment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 credit growth guidance 12%, deposit growth 10%, CASA 45%.
FY27 NIM guided at around 3.5%; management said it could be revised upward next quarter once retail yields recover.
RoA to be maintained around the current 1.37%; RoE around 16%; GNPA below 2.25%.
Employee cost expected at around INR500 crores per quarter for the next two quarters; full-year FY27 employee cost seen around INR2,500 crores or lower.
Credit cost guided at 0.1% to 0.2%, excluding ECL impact.
Business target of above INR5 lakh crores in three years from the current ~INR2.9 lakh crores; management said it would grow above system if system grows 16%.
capex_capacity: Capital raise of up to INR1,250 crores planned in FY27 at an opportune time, with Board and shareholder approval already obtained; RBI ECL framework effective 1 April 2027.
Management estimated five-year ECL provisioning of around INR1,600 to INR1,700 crores on RBI's base requirements.
Co-lending target of around INR1,000 crores for FY27, with Board approval up to INR5,000 crores; co-lending started only in Q4 FY26.
Zonal ARBs introduced as specialised recovery units.
End-to-end digitised loan journeys in place for all loans; TAT for corporate, mid-corporate and SME loans reduced substantially in Q4.
demand_pricing: Yield on advances fell due to 125 bps of RBI rate cuts in 2025 and higher-rated corporate lending at competitive rates; FY27 focus is on retail, which management expects to lift yields.
Deposit competition in J&K is intensifying, mainly in Srinagar and Jammu, while the bank holds about 80-85% share in smaller districts.
Management says the bank recovered some lost accounts in FY26; April 2026 business figures were the best of any April, per management.
Management said it has not found any sticky sector; no MFI exposure; all NBFC exposures are AAA-rated, mainly housing, public sector and gold loans.
SMA-2 rose to 0.71% in March 2026 from 0.35% a year earlier, but was down from 2.92% in December 2025.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall sharply, and what is the run rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Pension obligations are shifting to NPS and retirements have reduced headcount. Q4 employee cost was INR509 crores including a INR153 crore discount-rate reversal. Management expects about INR500 crores per quarter for the next two quarters and about INR2,500 crores for the full year, with some hiring of specialists.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall, and what was the Gramin Bank item?
qa_highlights.answer: A one-time INR180 crore impairment on the investment in J&K Gramin Bank, taken in other income after the NABARD-directed amalgamation of Ellaquai Dehati Bank (EDB). Management said it was a policy decision and occurred in the full year, not in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank grow faster than the system?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is conservative. Management said it would aim to grow above 16% if system growth reached 16%.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM improve, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects NIM to improve because deposit repricing benefits are yet to accrue. Retail income from J&K will take one to one-and-a-half quarters to regenerate. Management may revise NIM guidance upward next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost outlook beyond the next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost guided at 0.1% to 0.2% maximum for FY27, excluding ECL. Management said it cannot foresee credit cost above 1% over the next three to four years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated five-year ECL provisioning of INR1,600 to INR1,700 crores, using RBI base requirements, and said the actual number will depend on the bank's board-approved model.

risks_watch: ECL transition from 1 April 2027 with about INR1,600 to 1,700 crores of five-year provisioning and a capital raise of INR1,250 crores.
NIM recovery depends on retail yield improvement in J&K; management was not yet sure when retail returns would accrue.
Heavy financial-market (NBFC) book growth; concentration and co-lending scale-up.
Competitive pressure on deposits and loss of J&K market share (60% share vs 37% branch share).
SMA-2 uptick to 0.71% from 0.35% a year earlier.
Geopolitical risk in West Asia; World Bank cut India FY27 growth forecast to 6.6%.
Other-income volatility from trading income and one-off items such as the INR180 crore Gramin Bank impairment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on delivery and asset quality, but deliberately conservative on FY27 guidance, citing West Asia geopolitical risk. Management was openly cautious on NIM, attributing the miss to rate cuts and J&K retail income loss. It was evasive on the ECL quantum beyond its five-year estimate and on the long-term credit cost path.
key_quotes: While it may seem like we are under-promising, rest assured, that we will strive to over-deliver, like we did this year.
I would not categorize any segment as sticky.
I am unable to assess a credit cost which is more than 1% in the next three to four years.
The margins would be better, definitely better.

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 12% credit growth, 10% deposit growth and ~3.5% NIM, with no specific capacity, orders or contracts behind it; backing rests on retail focus, deposit share and April business momentum, so clarity is vague.
